title: PRISM benchmark report
description: Shape of benchmarks/out/run.json as written by benchmarks/run.py. Hardware is required: a latency number without the machine that produced it is not evidence, and a baseline comparison across different hardware is meaningless rather than merely imprecise.

profile.description: Only the release profile is release evidence. The smoke profile takes too few samples for a p95 to mean anything.

workload.description: Filename in benchmarks/workloads/. Two runs of different workloads are not comparable.

cold_start_ms.description: Reported, never gated, and never folded into a warm percentile.

peak_rss_bytes.description: Maximum resident memory over the process tree, sampled continuously on a background thread. A single reading taken when the run ends is not a peak: the maximum sits inside a measurement.

rss_sampling.description: How peak_rss_bytes was obtained, so a reader can tell a sampled maximum from a final reading.

final_rss_bytes.description: The end-of-run reading the sampler replaced, over the same process tree peak_rss_bytes covers. The two differ only in when the sample was taken, never in what was counted, so the gap between them is exactly what a final reading misses.

deadline.description: The workload's declared timeout against the worst warm measurement. FAIL is a recorded result: the adversarial workload is expected to breach it on current hardware, and the number is not moved to make the verdict green.

series_measured_under_seconds.description: Instrumentation, not a threshold. A ceiling cannot be recorded without observing past the deadline, so the series is taken under this timeout while the verdict is judged against declared_seconds.

pair_work.description: How much inference the run actually performed. pairs_total is the input shape; pairs_scored_by_nli is the work, and a pair counts as scored only when both directions were scored.

full_pair_space_asserted.description: True only for the adversarial workload, where falling short of the full 160 pairs fails the run.
